images.filename: Green Mill Cocktail Lounge Sign, Broadway, Uptown, Chicago, IL (54841201167).jpg
images.caption: Built in 1914 and renovated in 1922 and 1925, this Commercial-style building was designed by C. S. Michaelsen to serve as a commercial building and the home of the Green Mill Gardens, an outdoor beer garden that originally opened on the present site of the Uptown Theater in 1909.  The building originally contained a restaurant and ballroom, and an outdoor beer garden to the west, as well as a green windmill atop the building’s roof, which were removed when the Uptown Theater was constructed in 1925.  The building’s oldest sections are located at the south and west of the present structure, while the northeast corner was added during the 1922 renovations, filling in a front courtyard, and the original west wing of the building was demolished in 1925 to make way for the Uptown Theater.  The building continued to serve as a commercial building with a large two-story restaurant and dance hall in the western portion, which operated under various names during the 20th Century.  The building, additionally, underwent alterations in 1933, following a major fire, and at some point around the mid-20th Century, the ballroom and restaurant ceased to operate as a public venue, and were divided into smaller commercial spaces.  The building is clad in red brick with limestone trim, a modified first floor and parapet, replacement windows, and a decorative limestone surround at the former main entrance bay.  The building is one of the structures that comprises the Uptown Square Historic District, listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 2000, and designated a Chicago Landmark District in 2016.  Today, the building houses a variety of businesses, including the Green Mill Cocktail Lounge.
